questions.text: When Place order is pressed, Order calls Cart over HTTP and then sends ReserveStock as an event. If the Cart call fails or is slow, what does the customer see and what state is the order in?
questions.about: Create order, status PENDING_RESERVATION / HTTP get cart

questions.text: The diagram shows two arrows from the Outcome? decision to PAYMENT_DECLINED: one plain and one dotted event PaymentDeclined. How does Order actually learn about a decline?

Where does the 'customer told: these items are short' or 'payment declined' message get shown, given Place order is an HTTP call? Does the customer wait on that call, or is the result delivered some other way?
questions.about: Customer told: these items are short / Customer told: payment declined

questions.text: What if the order stays in PENDING_RESERVATION or AWAITING_PAYMENT because an event never gets handled (for example Inventory never answers)? What moves it forward or ends it?

For a success that arrives when the order is not AWAITING_PAYMENT, the refund arrow goes straight from the Order check to Ask provider for a FULL refund. What actually sends the refund request there, and is the stock reservation released in that case?
questions.about: Is the order still AWAITING_PAYMENT? - no branch

questions.text: How does a webhook get tied to the right order? And how does Payment turn the outcome into the PaymentSucceeded or PaymentDeclined event to Order, given the event is saved by the outbox in the same transaction?
questions.about: Webhook received / Save event id in inbox and update the payment record in ONE transaction

questions.text: The Customer emailed: order confirmed and Status CONFIRMED happen together with OrderConfirmed to Cart. Who sends the emails, and if Cart emptying fails or the email fails, what happens to the confirmed order?
The Expiry sweep has a dotted arrow to the reservation step. Does it also tell Order anything when it releases a hold, or does the order only find out when the late payment arrives?

answers.text: Order calls Cart before saving anything. If the call fails or times out, no order exists, the customer sees a try-again message and the cart is untouched. Reason: nothing has happened yet, so the simplest handling is to fail cleanly. Added to the first box and a new failure note.
The two arrows were a mistake in the diagram. Order learns of a decline only through the event PaymentDeclined, which Payment writes to its outbox. I removed the plain arrow.

Place order returns the order id at once. The customer's page polls Order for the status and shows the short-items or declined message from it. Emails come from Order. Polling is the simplest way to deliver a result that may take up to 30 minutes. Added to How to read.

PENDING_RESERVATION: a new Order sweep cancels it after 5 minutes as CANCELLED_TIMEOUT and sends ReleaseStock (harmless if no hold). No charge was requested yet, so this is safe. AWAITING_PAYMENT: the existing lost-webhook status check after about 35 minutes ends it. The 5 minutes is a proposal, listed as an open point.

The arrow was missing its trigger. Order sends the event RefundRequested, as it does after a failed claim. The label now says so. A cancelled or rejected order has no live hold (released on decline, never made on timeout or short stock, none after a failed claim), so nothing needs releasing. I also added: if the order is already CONFIRMED the event is ignored, so a confirmed order is never refunded.

Payment sends the order id as the charge reference when it charges, and the webhook carries it back, so Payment finds the payment record by it. The exact provider field is a detail left out of the file. The webhook transaction now also writes PaymentSucceeded or PaymentDeclined to the outbox, shown in the box and the duplicate-webhook note.

Order sends all customer emails after saving the status, with retries. A failed email never changes the order. If emptying the cart fails, the outbox redelivers OrderConfirmed until Cart succeeds, and the order stays CONFIRMED. The brief names no email service, so putting it in Order is my choice, to keep one fewer part.

No. The sweep tells nobody, because Order needs to know only when a payment arrives and the claim fails. Telling Order would add a mechanism the brief does not need. Stated in the sweep box and the late-success note.

questions.text: What is the cart's 'checkout attempt'? Who creates it and when, and how does it differ from a new attempt after a declined payment, which gets a new order id?
If the charge request to the provider times out or errors, who retries it, and what state is the payment record and the order in while that happens?
questions.about: Save payment record PENDING / ask provider to charge

questions.text: The hold lasts 10 minutes but the provider can take up to 30. What do customers with a slow payment normally experience, and is that the intended outcome?
questions.about: Inventory: Reserve ALL lines in one transaction, status HELD, expires in 10 minutes

questions.text: Between the 10-minute hold expiry and the 35-minute status check, what does the customer's page show for an order still AWAITING_PAYMENT? What triggers the status check, and which service owns that timer?

The sweep cancels an order after 5 minutes, but a late StockReserved is then ignored. Does the Order service also ignore a late StockShort, and what happens to the customer's page when the order is CANCELLED_TIMEOUT? Is there a customer message for it?
How does a consumer such as Order or Inventory recognise a redelivered event? Which id does it store, and is it saved in the same transaction as the state change?
questions.about: event ids already handled (Order) / Every consumer is idempotent

questions.text: Where does the refund amount come from and who knows the provider's charge to refund? Does a refund request for an order whose payment was only declined or never completed do anything?
questions.about: Ask provider for a FULL refund

answers.text: The attemptId is a random id the checkout page creates when it opens, and recreates after a failed order. Place order sends it and Order stores it with a unique key. Same id on a double click returns the same order; a new id after a decline makes a new order id. Client-generated is the simplest way to tell a double click from a deliberate retry. Explained in How to read.

Payment retries a few times with the same idempotency key. Payment record stays PENDING and the order stays AWAITING_PAYMENT. If it still gets no answer, the lost-webhook status check settles it. No new mechanism. The retry count is listed as an open point.

A payment slower than 10 minutes always ends in cancellation and a full refund, even if the stock is still free, because the claim checks the expiry. This follows the brief (unclaimed stock goes back on sale after 10 minutes) and no re-reserve. Stated in the late-success note.

The page shows 'waiting for payment' for AWAITING_PAYMENT until a claim fails or the status check settles it. The Payment service owns the timer: a minute-by-minute sweep over PENDING payment records older than about 35 minutes. Added to the Lost webhook note.

Yes, a late StockShort is ignored too, because every handler checks the order's status. CANCELLED_TIMEOUT now has a page message: could not process the order, cart unchanged, try again. Added a box and arrow to the diagram.

Every event carries a unique event id. Each consumer (Order, Inventory, Payment) stores handled ids in the same transaction as its state change and skips ids it has seen. Stated in How to read and added to the stores table and Inventory box.

The amount is the full amount from the order snapshot, carried in RefundRequested. Payment finds the provider charge id on its own payment record by order id. If the record is not SUCCEEDED (declined or never completed) the request does nothing. Added to the refund box and the failed refund note.

teachbacks.text:
1. Customer presses Place order. The checkout page has already made a random attemptId when it opened. The page calls the Order service over HTTP and sends the attemptId. The document does not say what else is sent, such as a cart id or customer id.

2. Order calls Cart over HTTP to get the cart's lines and prices. Cart returns them and does not change the cart. If this call fails, Order creates nothing and the customer is asked to try again. The cart is untouched.

3. Order creates an order with status PENDING_RESERVATION. It saves a frozen snapshot of the lines and prices, so later cart or price changes never touch the order. It stores the attemptId under a unique key. A double click (same attemptId) returns the same order. Order replies to the page at once with the orderId (created when Place order is pressed). The page then polls Order for the order's status.

4. Order publishes the event ReserveStock (orderId and lines). Events are written through a transactional outbox: the state change and the event are saved in one database transaction, and a relay publishes the event afterwards. Every event has a unique id. Each consumer saves the ids it has handled in the same transaction as its state change and ignores an id it has already seen. Handlers also check the current status and ignore events that no longer fit.

5. Inventory checks whether every line is in stock.
   - If any line is short, it reserves nothing and sends StockShort with the list of short items. Order sets REJECTED_SHORT_STOCK and stores the short items. The page shows which items are short. Nothing is charged, nothing is requested from Payment, and the cart is unchanged.
   - If all lines are available, it reserves all of them in one transaction. The reservation is HELD with a 10-minute expiry, and Inventory sends StockReserved.

6. Failure case: Inventory never answers. An Order sweep runs every minute. Any order that has been PENDING_RESERVATION for over 5 minutes becomes CANCELLED_TIMEOUT. The sweep sends ReleaseStock, which does nothing if there is no hold. The page shows "could not process the order, try again". A late StockReserved or StockShort is ignored because the order is no longer pending. A late hold lapses by itself after 10 minutes.

7. On StockReserved, Order sets AWAITING_PAYMENT. The page shows "waiting for payment". Order sends ChargeRequested (orderId and the total from the snapshot).

8. Payment receives ChargeRequested. It saves a payment record as PENDING and asks the provider to charge. The idempotency key is the orderId, and the orderId is also sent as the charge reference. On error or timeout it retries a few times with the same key, so a retry cannot double-charge. If there is still no answer, the order stays AWAITING_PAYMENT and the lost-webhook check (step 15) settles it.

9. The provider charges the card. This takes seconds, up to 30 minutes. It sends the result by webhook, and it may send the same webhook twice.

10. Payment handles the webhook. It verifies the signature and finds the payment record by the orderId reference. It checks whether the provider's event id is already in its inbox.
   - If the id is already there, it does nothing and replies 200 OK so the provider stops resending.
   - If not, in ONE transaction it saves the event id in the inbox, updates the payment record, and writes PaymentSucceeded or PaymentDeclined to the outbox. Payment status changes are one-way, so SUCCEEDED cannot become DECLINED.

11. Declined path. Order receives PaymentDeclined and sets PAYMENT_DECLINED. It sends ReleaseStock, and Inventory releases the hold (it does nothing if the hold has lapsed). The page tells the customer the payment was declined. The cart is unchanged. The page makes a new attemptId, so a retry creates a new order with a new orderId and a new idempotency key.

12. Success path. Order receives PaymentSucceeded and checks whether it is still AWAITING_PAYMENT.
   - If yes, it sends ClaimStock. Inventory checks, in one transaction, that the reservation is still HELD and not past expiry. If so, it sets CLAIMED (stock is sold, permanent) and sends StockClaimed. Order sets CONFIRMED and emails the customer. Order then sends OrderConfirmed, and Cart empties the cart. This is the only place the cart is emptied. Emptying is idempotent, and if it fails the outbox redelivers until it works, with the order staying CONFIRMED meanwhile.
   - If the order is already CONFIRMED, the event is ignored.
   - If the order is CANCELLED_* or REJECTED_*, Order sends RefundRequested for a full refund. There is no hold to release.

13. Late success after the hold lapsed. An Inventory expiry sweep runs every minute. It turns HELD rows past their expiry into RELEASED, puts the stock back on sale, and does not tell Order. Claim and expiry are mutually exclusive, so a reservation is either claimed or released, never both. Until the claim fails, the page keeps showing "waiting for payment". If the claim fails, Inventory replies StockClaimFailed. Order sets CANCELLED_OUT_OF_STOCK, emails "cancelled as out of stock, full refund on its way", and sends RefundRequested for the full amount from the snapshot. There is no re-reservation. So a payment that takes longer than 10 minutes always ends in a cancellation and a refund.

14. Refund. Payment receives RefundRequested. It refunds only if the payment record is SUCCEEDED, otherwise it does nothing. It saves the refund record before calling the provider and asks for a full refund with the idempotency key "refund + orderId", using the record's charge id.
   - If the provider accepts, the record is DONE and Payment sends RefundCompleted. Order records the refund as done and the customer is emailed "refund issued".
   - On error or timeout, the record is RETRYING and is retried with growing delays. A sweeper re-picks unfinished refunds, which also covers a crash between the save and the call.
   - After N failed attempts the record becomes REFUND_FAILED and operations is alerted. The record stays open and keeps being retried, and it is never dropped. Retry resumes after operations fixes the cause. Refund results that arrive by webhook use the same inbox and duplicate check.

15. Lost webhook. A Payment sweep runs every minute. It finds payment records still PENDING after about 35 minutes and asks the provider for the charge's status. It processes the answer through the same inbox path as a webhook. "No such charge" counts as declined.

16. Emails. Order sends every customer email after it saves the new status. A failed email is retried and never changes the order.
gaps: The document does not say what the Place order request contains besides attemptId (for example, how Order knows which customer's cart to fetch), or how the page authenticates.

It does not say how the page learns the orderId and starts polling, or what the polling interval is. It also does not say what the page shows for a status the document gives no wording for. It does not say whether REJECTED_SHORT_STOCK, PAYMENT_DECLINED and CANCELLED_TIMEOUT cause any email.
It does not say what the customer sees while the order is PENDING_RESERVATION, or what the page shows after CONFIRMED beyond the confirmation email.

It does not say what happens if Order receives StockShort or StockReserved while it is not PENDING_RESERVATION other than ignoring it, for example how a StockReserved that arrives after CANCELLED_TIMEOUT is handled. The late hold lapses after 10 minutes, but nothing is said about a hold that has already been reserved.

The flowchart's PaymentSucceeded or PaymentDeclined arriving for an order not in AWAITING_PAYMENT is described only for success. The document does not say what Order does with a late PaymentDeclined when the order is not AWAITING_PAYMENT.
It does not say what happens if ClaimStock is sent but the claim reply is never received, or how the order is settled if StockClaimed or StockClaimFailed is lost.

It does not say whether RefundCompleted for a refund that was triggered from a REJECTED or CANCELLED order also sends the 'refund issued' email, or what Order does with the refund record beyond marking it done.
The document does not say how the relay and the message broker deliver events (ordering guarantees, retry policy for redelivery) beyond 'the outbox redelivers until it works'.

It does not say which fields Payment stores for retry state, or how the Payment sweep for PENDING charges is reconciled with the charge-request retries at the 35-minute mark relative to the 30-minute provider maximum.
The open points leave unspecified: N (refund attempts), the retry delays, who receives the REFUND_FAILED alert, and the number of charge retries.
